Subject: Indexing Alliance: Data Mesh + Vector Store Integration Charter

Hi Lena, Tom —

Thanks for taking the call last week. As discussed, we want to formalize a lightweight alliance between Redwood, Foundry Labs (implementation partner), and Pinecone to standardize how our customers onboard a data-mesh-style content layer that uses S3 as canonical storage with pgvector or Pinecone as the operational vector index and an explicit S3 fallback for archival queries.

Attached: a first-pass charter (indexing-alliance-charter-v1.pdf) and a security quicklist (security-quicklist.xlsx). The charter covers: scope, roles (GTM, engineering handoff, success metrics), a minimal MOU, and an initial mutual action plan (MAP).

Immediate asks:
- Can Foundry confirm a single technical lead for integration work?
- Tom — can Pinecone share a compact compatibility matrix (vector dims, index types, supported metadata fields) and a preferred contact for SRE/ingest patterns?
- Redwood: we’ll draft a 60-day pilot MAP and include a canary rollout + S3 fallback acceptance tests.

Goal: run a 6-week pilot with 1 customer (mutual customer or sandbox) that demonstrates: ingestion throughput 100 QPS sustained ingest bursts, sub-50ms per-query P95 for 128-dim vectors, and transparent fallback to S3 within 2s for cold hits.

Open questions for the group: contractual minimal terms for handling persisted embeddings, who owns the canonical index snapshot, and SLA alignment for cross-provider failover.

Proposed next step: 30-minute scoping on Thursday 2026-09-30 09:00 PT. If that works, I’ll send calendar invite and a short MAP doc in Drive for collaborative edits.

Thanks — Rafael

Thanks Rafael and Lena — great to see this coming together. I’m Tom (Pinecone integration lead). Short answers and a compatibility file attached (pinecone-compat-matrix.csv).

Notes:
- We support dense vectors up to 1536 dims, multiple index types (sparse/dense hybrid in beta); metadata keys are free-form but we recommend a normalized id + namespace + timestamp.
- For cold fallback testing: sample size should be representative of your 95th-percentile collection size. For many customers, 2–5M vectors is a realistic test. For >10M we recommend sharding by namespace and validating warm-up behavior.
- Ingest patterns: bulk batched uploads (1000 vectors/file) are the fastest during initial backfill; streaming ingest is fine for steady-state. We’ll share a short SRE checklist for the pilot.

Action items from Pinecone:
1) Share SRE checklist (will do by EOD 2026-09-29).
2) Provide a test dataset (anonymized) that we can use in our sandboxes once Foundry confirms test vectors.

Attachment: pinecone-compat-matrix.csv

Reviewed the charter and Pinecone notes. A few operational clarifications from Redwood’s side:
- Canary plan: we’ll own the canary rollout for live routing (route 5% traffic to index A, 95% to fallback with tracing). Acceptance: P95 latency <= 80ms for the canary slice and no more than 1% query error increase.
- Oncall: Ben can act as primary during pilot (oncall rotation will be documented in the Runbook). Monica will handle billing/commercial touchpoints and can own HubSpot tagging for the co-sell lead.
- Security: we require short answers on encryption-at-rest for any partner-supplied snapshots and confirmation of retention policies for vector metadata. See security-quicklist.xlsx attached.

I’ve added a small technical appendix to the Drive MAP (same Drive link). Rafael, I recommend we capture the pilot acceptance criteria as discrete Jira tasks (VSTOR-342 is the umbrella). Can Foundry add estimated engineering effort per MAP milestone?
